inspection.tool: Existing local PEReader/System.Reflection.Metadata inspector, without loading or executing target code

reusedREAMetadataEvidence.limitation: REA recognized the managed PE and verified artifact identity, but stopped metadata decoding at its representation budget. Selected IL and MVID below come from the separate bounded local System.Reflection.Metadata inspector.

findings.claim: Configured body, mouth and eye clips loop on tracks 0, 1 and 2, respectively. Catchlight animation is authored inside each configured eye clip; this class has no dedicated catchlight track.
findings.proof: ApplyAnimation loads Body/Mouth/Eye/Blink separately; PlayTrackAnimation IL_0013 ldc.i4.1 immediately precedes SetAnimation; ESpineTrack constants are Body=0,Mouth=1,Eye=2.

findings.claim: Identical clip names retain their existing track clocks across expression IDs, including a currently playing blink when the eye and blink names stay unchanged.
findings.proof: String equality causes immediate return before native SetAnimation or timer mutation.

findings.claim: The first blink begins after a random 3–6 seconds. Further 3–6 second delays start at blink start, so timing is start-to-start rather than blink-finish-to-start.
findings.proof: ScheduleBlink computes 3 + Random.Shared.NextSingle()*3; PlayBlink calls it immediately after queuing eye playback, without waiting for completion.

findings.claim: A blink replaces track 2 once; the open-eye loop then starts again at phase zero after the authored blink duration. Body and mouth clocks continue.

Changing the blink mapping cancels its timer; when any blink has started, StopBlinking reinstates the currently mapped open-eye loop at phase zero. Empty blink names store null and disable scheduling. Same blink mappings preserve the timer.
findings.proof: StopBlinking is called before changed mapping assignment; null/empty stored as null; ScheduleBlink requires BlinkEnabled,currentEye,currentBlink,character ID and active visible root.

findings.claim: There is no completion callback that resets IsEyeTrackBlinking in this class; it persists until StopBlinking or ResetRuntimeState.
findings.proof: These are the only stfld uses of IsEyeTrackBlinking in the complete existing class inventory.

findings.claim: Clearing an optional eye/mouth track uses an immediate empty animation. Ordinary valid expression changes never clear all tracks or reset the entire skeleton. Load/Reset performs whole state cleanup.
findings.proof: ClearTrack calls SetEmptyAnimation(track,0) and clears its cached name. Load calls ClearTracks and SetToSetupPose; Reset invokes ResetRuntimeState, ResetAppearance, StopTalking and StopBlinking.

findings.claim: Normal playback has speed 1; explicit playback-rate and pause requests control the shared Spine time scale.
findings.proof: .ctor assigns SpinePlaybackRate=1. SetPaused uses zero or current rate; SetPlaybackRate forwards supplied rate when not paused.

findings.claim: Stage portraits and dialogue avatars use the same VisualNovelSpineCharacter implementation with independent instances/transforms and blink enabled.
findings.proof: Stage factory acquires SolarSchoolCharacterSpineItem.Character, constructed as VisualNovelSpineCharacter, enables blinking, then Load. Dialogue owns another CharacterSpineItem.Character, enables blinking in startup, applies its HeadIconTransform and calls ApplyAnimation.

limitations: Static managed IL establishes controller requests and their order, not exact native Unreal/LGUI framebuffer output or implicit native mix settings.
The controller is installed resource 3.8.9; local authored flowstate/expression data has the recorded resource 3.8 source scope.
Catchlight shape, easing, deformation, draw order, and per-eye/per-expression coverage must be established from each actual Spine skeleton and atlas, not this controller inventory.
